- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 2–4% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns bullish after 2–3 days, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 2–5% when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply a +2% bias correction for such periods.
- If true outcome shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive days >70), model fails to capture it; increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until momentum flattens.
